english.title: Forge insurance document with intent to deceive
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) with intent to deceive, forged

(A)_[a certificate of insurance.]_
(B)_[a certificate of security under Part VI of The Road Traffic Act 1988.]_
(C)_[a document produced as evidence of insurance pursuant to regulation 6 of the Motor Vehicles (Compulsory Insurance) (No.2) Regulations 1973.]_
(D)_[a document issued under regulations made under section 165(2)(a) of the Road Traffic Act 1988]_
english.legislation: Contrary to section 173(1) of the Road Traffic Act 1988 and Schedule 2 to the Road Traffic Offenders Act 1988.

english.notes:
(i) See also associated offence wordings as follows: H60, H62, H64, H85, H94, H95 H96, H97, H3002, H3004 and H3030.
(ii) From 1st November 2019, the Motor Vehicles (Compulsory Insurance) (Miscellaneous Amendments) Regulations 2019 (SI 2019/1047) removed the current securities regime, which was used as an alternative to conventional motor insurance. A two-year transitional period applied to existing securities and deposits; this meant that new securities could not be issued, however, it did not prevent individuals renewing current securities - as long as they were valid until 1st November 2021. From 1st November 2021 compulsory motor insurance is required. See offence H100116.

other.penalty:
SUMMARY: A fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.

INDICTMENT: Two years imprisonment.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
